one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Four-decade-old B2B engineering company designing and manufacturing hydraulic fittings (11,000+ SKUs) for OEMs and distributors across construction, farming, automotive, injection moulding and hydraulic-systems customers in India and eleven export markets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Hy-Tech Engineers designs, manufactures and supplies standard and customer-specified hydraulic fittings - DIN-metric, JIC flared and flareless, O-Ring Face Seal (ORFS) and conversion fittings - from six manufacturing facilities in Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh, with backward integration into forging at its Nashik Unit. It sells business-to-business, combining direct engagement with OEMs and industrial customers (170 direct customers in Fiscal 2026, 88.42% of revenue from operations) with a network of 7 distributors and distribution partners in India and overseas. As of March 31, 2026 its portfolio consists of more than 11,000 SKUs and it holds certifications (IRIS, DRDO approval) that open the railways and defence sectors.

group_structure.title: Group structure (subsidiaries / JV / related parties)
group_structure.body:
- Hy-Tech USA Inc. — Group Company and Promoter Group entity (Richmond, Virginia, USA): Exclusive distributor of the Company's hydraulic fittings for North America, Canada and Brazil under agreement dated April 1, 2022. Direct sales to it were 3.54%, 3.04% and 3.95% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Customers sourced by it contributed ₹338.71 million (FY26), ₹319.59 million (FY25) and ₹283.77 million (FY24). Engaged in a similar line of business - flagged as a conflict-of-interest risk (Risk Factor 14). Ceased to be a subsidiary following a share buy-back under agreement dated February 18, 2022.
- Hy-Tech Fluid Power Private Limited — Group Company (Thane, Maharashtra): Related party to whom the Company extends credit; flagged in Risk Factor 18 on receivables from related parties.
- NR Hytech Engineers Private Limited — Group Company (Kesurdi, Khandala, Satara, Maharashtra): Hemant Tukaram Mondkar and Surekha Hemant Mondkar hold other directorships in it.
- Hy-Tech ACR Private Limited (also referred to as Hytech ACR Private Limited) — Erstwhile Subsidiary: Ceased to be a subsidiary with effect from January 20, 2026 on voluntary strike-off by the RoC. Incurred losses on a standalone basis: PBT (0.13) mn FY26, (0.03) mn FY25, (0.46) mn FY24, with negative operating cash flows. Included in the Restated Consolidated Financial Information for the periods covered.
- Fasto Engineering Private Limited — Promoter Group member; other directorship of Hemant Tukaram Mondkar: Co-accused with Promoter Hemant Tukaram Mondkar in two pending complaints filed by the Government Labour Officer and Inspector, Thane (March 02, 2026 under the Minimum Wages Act, 1948; April 09, 2026 under the Payment of Wages Act, 1936).
- CARE Analytics and Advisory Private Limited (CareEdge Research) — Independent industry consultant: Author of the 'Industry Research Report on Hydraulic Fittings Industry' dated August 2026, commissioned and paid for by the Company exclusively for the Offer. Not a related party of the Company, Promoters, Directors, KMP, Senior Management or the BRLM.

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Backward integration into forging at the Nashik Unit, which manufactures forged components used as raw material by all the other manufacturing units. "We operate with backward integration at our Nashik Unit which is equipped to manufacture forged components which are in turn used at our other facilities to manufacture hydraulic fittings. As of March 31, 2026, we have a total installed capacity of forging capacity of 3,120.00 MT per annum at our Nashik Unit and a manufacturing capacity of 483.00 lakhs pieces per annum of hydraulic fittings across all our other facilities. This backward integration reduces reliance on external suppliers and supports cost efficiency, lead time reduction, and quality control." The Thane, Shirwal, Kavathe and Pithampur units each operate as independent, non-inter-dependent manufacturing units, but all depend on the Nashik Unit for supply of forged components. Manufacturing operations encompass die-designing, forging, heat treatment, machining, plating and inspection and testing, primarily conducted in-house, together with in-house design capability; production infrastructure includes CNC machines, multi-spindle machines, transfer machines, vertical machining centers, thread rolling and centerless grinding machines. A decentralized cell-based manufacturing model is followed, with operations organized into smaller self-contained cells with dedicated oversight for production, quality and design support, plant heads responsible for operational performance and central teams for procurement and strategic planning. On the inbound side, the primary raw material is steel (carbon steel, alloy steel and stainless steel in bars and forgings), majorly sourced from Indian suppliers - imported materials were Rs 3.05 million, Rs 5.68 million and Rs 1.03 million (0.45%, 0.92% and 0.22% of total cost of materials purchased) in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Raw materials are procured on purchase orders with no purchase agreements or firm commitments; multiple sources are generally maintained for each major raw material. On the outbound side, a dual-channel model combines direct sales to OEMs and industrial customers with a distributor network, including Promoter Group entity Hy-Tech USA Inc. as exclusive distributor for North America, Canada and Brazil providing local fulfilment and technical support. Quality control comprises a dedicated team of 22 professionals as on March 31, 2026.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Revenue mix across geographies and channels - exports were 29.37% and domestic 70.63% of FY26 revenue; direct/OEM sales 88.42% with the balance from distributors. Export contracts may carry higher margins but bring currency risk and stricter delivery and quality compliance; domestic sales offer lower logistics cost and faster turnaround. Shifts in this mix move realisations, the working capital cycle and the margin profile.
- Sectoral demand cycles - performance is tied to investment and replacement cycles and infrastructure outlays in construction equipment, earthmoving, agricultural machinery and industrial hydraulics; a capex slowdown would hit order volumes, plant utilisation and revenue visibility.
- Customer concentration - approximately 30.26% of FY26 revenues came from the top five customers; loss of any due to insourcing, cost rationalisation or design change would materially affect revenue and profitability. Expanding the customer base and end-user industries is stated as a key strategic priority.
- Input cost volatility - black steel and mild steel are the dominant input cost. Price variation clauses exist in customer contracts but negotiation lags and limited pass-through, particularly in export agreements, can compress gross margins and raise working capital requirements.
- Unhedged foreign currency exposure - export receivables are denominated primarily in USD and EUR; the Company does not engage in active hedging or offsetting imports, leaving margins exposed to exchange-rate volatility.
- Operational efficiency and capacity utilisation - operating leverage depends on utilisation across the Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh facilities; sub-optimal utilisation causes under-absorption of fixed overheads and hits EBITDA margins. Lean manufacturing, line balancing and preventive maintenance are the stated levers.
- Execution of capital expenditure plans - timely commissioning of automation, machining capacity and testing infrastructure is critical to avoid cost overruns, bottlenecks and delayed customer qualification, and drives future revenue scalability, working capital deployment and asset turnover.
- Regulatory and customer-audit compliance - environmental, labour, industrial safety and EXIM requirements plus customer quality certifications (ISO/TS standards) and traceability norms; delays in approvals such as CTO/CTE can raise compliance cost or disrupt operations.
- Tariff and trade-policy uncertainty in North America and Europe - new or higher import duties, withdrawal of preferential access or non-tariff barriers could hurt export price competitiveness, customer ordering patterns and margins.
- Single operating segment - the Company operates in one segment (hydraulic fittings), so no separate segment reporting is made under Ind AS 108; business is stated to be neither seasonal nor cyclical in nature.
- Supplier concentration - top 10 suppliers accounted for 65.61%, 54.78% and 65.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Enhancing manufacturing capabilities - install high-precision machinery (CNC turning centres, thread rolling machines, CNC vertical machining centres), automation and improved process integration at Shirwal, Kavathe and Pithampur Unit-I
- Strategic diversification into high-growth sectors - deepen the recently entered defence and railways verticals leveraging IRIS certification and DRDO approval
- Diversification into the valve segment through both organic initiatives and inorganic avenues, leveraging existing end-industries and distribution channels without significant incremental fixed investment
- Continued expansion of the distribution network - increase the number of distributors, enter new domestic and international geographies, deepen wallet share with existing distributors, introduce distributor-specific incentive programs and a customer feedback mechanism
- Focus to increase the customer base in international markets - maintain existing OEM relationships, add new direct customers and distributors, invest in logistics and localised support to cut lead times, participate in international trade shows and build digital and localised marketing presence
- Continued focus on cost optimisation and operational efficiency - leverage scale, supplier relationships and enhanced backward integration; lean methodologies and waste reduction; solar panels installed at Kavathe and Shirwal and effluent treatment plants at all facilities
- Expand the SKU portfolio to drive wallet share with existing distributors and direct customers

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The Company intends to expand existing hydraulic-fittings capacity at three of its five fittings units - Shirwal Unit and Kavathe Unit (Satara, Maharashtra) and Pithampur Unit-I (Dhar, Madhya Pradesh) - which it says offer the physical space and operational relevance for scaling output. The expansion is machinery-led rather than greenfield: new CNC turning centres, thread rolling machines and CNC vertical machining centres are to be installed to raise throughput, shorten production cycles, improve precision and increase capacity to introduce new SKUs. Against installed capacity as on March 31, 2026 of 144.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Shirwal (utilisation 70.83%), 192.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Kavathe (utilisation 60.42%) and 52.00 lakh pieces p.a. at Pithampur Unit-I (utilisation 84.62%), the proposed additional capacity is 64.80, 79.20 and 43.20 lakh pieces p.a. respectively, taking enhanced capacity to 208.80, 271.20 and 95.20 lakh pieces p.a. - increases of 45.00%, 41.25% and 83.08%, subject to timely commissioning and as certified by an Independent Chartered Engineer on August 5, 2026. The stated rationale is rising demand for hydraulic fittings across sectors and geographies, the need to support entry into defence and railways, and the ability to serve expanded distribution reach. ₹299.66 million of the Net Proceeds (inclusive of GST) is earmarked for this capital expenditure, to be deployed ₹50.00 million in Fiscal 2027 and ₹249.66 million in Fiscal 2028; over the past three Fiscals the Company invested an average of ₹262.42 million per annum in plant and machinery. The Company flags that it has not yet placed orders for the machinery (Risk Factor 11) and that the expansion may not materialise as expected (Risk Factor 17). Backward integration continues to sit at the Nashik Unit (3,120 MT p.a. of forgings, largely captive), which supplies all fittings units - no expansion is proposed there.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Integrated in-house operations spanning die-designing, forging, heat treatment, machining, plating and inspection/testing, with backward integration at the Nashik Unit supplying forgings to all fittings units
- Breadth and pace of product development - over 11,000 SKUs, with 880 new SKUs added in Fiscal 2026, 1,676 in Fiscal 2025 and 2,206 in Fiscal 2024
- Diversified customer base and dual-channel reach - 170 direct customers in FY26 (152 FY25, 144 FY24) plus 7 distributors and distribution partners, reducing dependence on any single channel or vertical
- High customer retention - revenues from repeat customers were 95.10% of consolidated revenue from operations in FY26 (95.20% FY25, 91.20% FY24), from 114 repeat customers
- Established global presence - exports to eleven countries (USA, Belgium, Poland, Russia, Brazil, Italy, Saudi Arabia, Hungary, UAE, Thailand, Germany), 29.37% of FY26 revenue from operations
- Certification-led access to regulated sectors - ISO 9001/14001/45001, IATF 16949, IRIS (ISO/TS 22163:2017) and DRDO approval opening railways and defence
- Decentralised cell-based manufacturing model with plant-head accountability, supporting flexibility, cost discipline and customer-specific alignment
- Experienced promoter-led leadership - Hemant Tukaram Mondkar, IIT Bombay alumnus, with over four decades in the hydraulic fittings industry
- Six facilities across Maharashtra and Madhya Pradesh strategically located in western and central India with multi-modal transport access

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Customer concentration with no long-term contracts — Top 10 customers contributed 45.32%, 42.02% and 48.72% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024; the top five were approximately 30.26% in FY26 and the single largest customer, Tompkins Industries Inc, 9.34%. The Company does not enter into long-term arrangements with customers, so volumes are re-won order by order.
- Export dependence concentrated on the USA, with unhedged currency exposure — Exports were 29.37%, 28.30% and 33.14% of total revenues in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024, of which the USA alone contributed 21.42%, 22.85% and 24.56%. Receivables are largely USD and EUR denominated and the Company does not actively hedge or offset with imports; it separately flags exposure to uncertain tariff structures in North America and Europe.
- Supplier concentration and raw-material price pass-through — Top 10 suppliers accounted for 65.61%, 54.78% and 65.49% of total purchases in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024. Black/mild steel is the dominant input; price variation clauses exist but negotiation lags and limited pass-through, particularly in export agreements, compress gross margins.
- Execution risk on the Net Proceeds-funded expansion, with machinery orders not yet placed — ₹299.66 million of Net Proceeds is earmarked for capacity expansion at Kavathe, Shirwal and Pithampur Unit-I, but the Company confirms it has not placed orders for the machinery; delay in ordering or vendor delivery may cause time and cost overruns, and the deployment has not been appraised by any bank or financial institution.
- Capacity under-utilisation risk, amplified by the proposed expansion — Blended capacity utilisation (excluding Nashik) was 70.55% in FY26, 66.86% in FY25 and 73.42% in FY24 - it fell in FY25 before recovering. Kavathe already ran at only 60.42% in FY26 and is nonetheless to be expanded by 41.25%, so incremental capacity must find demand to avoid under-absorption of fixed overheads.
- Single-point backward-integration dependency on the Nashik Unit, alongside geographic concentration in Maharashtra — The Nashik Unit is the sole internal source of forgings, a raw material for all five hydraulic-fittings units; the RHP states the fittings units are dependent on its supply, so a shutdown there propagates across the network. Separately, four of six facilities sit in Maharashtra and generated 77.64%, 77.27% and 77.43% of revenue from operations in Fiscals 2026, 2025 and 2024.
- Related-party and conflict-of-interest exposure through Promoter Group entities — Promoter Group member Hy-Tech USA Inc. is engaged in a similar line of business (distribution of hydraulic fittings), is the exclusive North America/Canada/Brazil distributor, and accounted for 3.54% of FY26 revenue from operations while sourcing customers contributing a further ₹338.71 million. The Company also extends credit to related party Hy-Tech Fluid Power Private Limited, creating receivables-recovery risk.
- Working capital and receivables intensity — Trade receivables turnover was only 3.96x in FY26 (3.91x FY25, 3.47x FY24) and inventory turnover 2.44x, against an outstanding aggregate borrowing of ₹407.76 million as on June 30, 2026; net capital turnover fell from 4.87x in FY24 to 2.92x in FY26, indicating a lengthening working capital cycle relative to sales.
